stemMd: Which model best explains electrical conduction in a metal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All electrons are fixed in individual water molecules.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every atom becomes an isolated gas molecule.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Delocalised electrons can move through a lattice of positive ion cores.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Only neutrons travel from atom to atom.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The metal must first dissolve to conduct.

explanationMd: Metallic bonding includes mobile, delocalised electrons. They respond to an electric field while the ion cores remain in the solid lattice, explaining conduction without melting or dissolving.

distractorRationale.d: Neutrons do not carry electric charge.
distractorRationale.a: A pure metal is not a lattice of water molecules.
